expected.rationale: Deliberately contested pre-registration. Quantitative strokes-gained analysis (Scott Fawcett/DECADE, cited via Golf Digest) finds going for the drivable green historically nets ~897-under vs. 130-over relative to laying up — a clear statistical edge for BOMBER. But Golf.com, The Fried Egg, and SI.com independently argue the small, elevated, false-fronted green was hardened specifically against power, with average drives of 280+ yards still only producing 53.9% GIR in one cited week. Registering BOMBER on the stronger quantitative signal, but flagging this as a real toss-up rather than a confident single pick.
sources: Golf Digest, 'Why more players are going for the green at Riviera's 10th' (Scott Fawcett/DECADE data)
Golf.com, "'I would have taken par on the tee'"
The Fried Egg, 'Bringing Showtime Back: The 10th at Riviera'
SI.com, "Riviera's 10th holds key in distance issue"

approximations: the green's near-right-angle (~45 degree) orientation to the fairway and its false front are not modeled by the sim's flat circular green primitive; represented only via a laterally offset, scaled-down green
the cross/layup bunker at ~199 yards is approximated as a single wide coffin bunker at an estimated, not surveyed, position
disagreement: Pre-registered as contested (see expected.rationale), so this outcome was anticipated rather than a clean model failure. Also consistent with the shared root cause on augusta-13: at this short 315-yard length, going for the green means high effort for everyone, and STRAIGHT's structurally lower base dispersion coefficient wins the resulting proximity contest even against a green some sources describe as favoring touch over power -- which is itself one of the two real published views on this hole. Field average (3.90) vs. published (4.09) is within the plausibility threshold.
